title: PulseGuard: continuous micro-eval orchestration for safe batch/cache applies
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a lightweight, continuously running micro-eval orchestration (PulseGuard) that validates batching/caching config recommendations before and during apply. The goal is to detect small but meaningful quality regressions tied to cost optimizations and enable safe automated rollback or human-in-the-loop pause. This ticket covers orchestration glue, acceptance thresholds, observability hooks, and a minimal runbook for on-call responders.
acceptance_criteria: PulseGuard runs a 60-second micro-eval suite for any candidate batch/cache config change in the sandbox canary and produces a pass/fail signal within 5 minutes of apply start.

Signal combines semantic similarity (embedding delta), rank-preservation (nDCG on re-ranking prompts), and token-level BLEU/ROUGE where applicable. A composite score is calculated and compared to thresholds in the config.
If the composite score drops below the configured threshold, the system triggers a safe rollback policy or creates a P0 runbook alert depending on severity settings.
Human audit link (Drive/Confluence) and the failing golden prompt examples are automatically attached to the rollback ticket and Slack alert.
PulseGuard exposes a per-rollout dashboard panel showing trendlines, last-run composite score, and historical canary passes/fails for the applied config version.
implementation_notes: Orchestration will be implemented as a thin controller in the autotune service that triggers pre-defined micro-eval bundles stored in the evals repo.
Micro-eval bundles will be < 30 queries: a mix of short golden prompts, typical low-latency user prefixes, and 5 targeted re-rank pairs for ranking workloads.
Compute budget capped per-run: use dedicated small worker pool (cpu-heavy inference with cached KV prefixes) to keep cost predictable.
Composite scoring: normalize each metric to 0-1, weighted: semantic_sim(0.5), rank_ndcg(0.3), token_fidelity(0.2). Configurable per-team.

Use embedding model 'embed-legacy-512' for delta computations to avoid circularly using the same generation model when measuring similarity. If the deployed model family changes, fall back to the pinned embedding model in the project config.
Store golden prompts with metadata: intent, length_bucket, last_human_review, owner. New golden prompts require a SMITH APPROVAL label before they are used for automatic rollouts.
rollback_playbook: Severity classification: composite drop > 0.12 = automatic rollback; drop 0.06-0.12 = canary pause + human review; drop < 0.06 = annotate and continue.

Automatic rollback flow: cancel remaining canary traffic, switch routing to previous rollout variant, create rollback change event in the audit log, emit Slack incident with summary and link to failing items.

Human review flow: create a priority ticket in Linear with failing golden prompts attached, mark assignee from autotune-oncall rotation, wait up to 30 minutes for owner to acknowledge before auto-rollback triggers.

Post-rollback diagnostics: collect token-level diffs, top-5 embedding nearest neighbors for diverging responses, CPU/GPU utilization during canary, and profiler snapshot. Attach artifacts to the rollback ticket.
If rollback is triggered, run extended evaluation (full eval suite) automatically and schedule a retrospective with the config proposer.
runbook_steps: 1) Alert received in Slack and P0 Linear created by PulseGuard.
2) Oncall inspects dashboard: composite score, metric breakdown, and the five failing golden prompts.
3) If autrollback triggered, verify traffic switch completed and confirm no downstream errors. Close the incident and tag the original change with 'rolled-back-pulseguard'.
4) If human-review required, assign to owner, run quick manual checks in console sandbox, and either approve continuation or escalate to auto-rollback.
5) Document findings in the change's Confluence page and mark corrective action (increase threshold, remove problematic golden prompt, tighten example length bounds).
test_results_summary: Nightly dry-run against historical canary logs (last 14 days) showed PulseGuard would have caught 7 regressions previously undetected by unit tests: median composite drop 0.09.
Simulated noisy inputs: false positive rate measured at ~1.8% with current thresholds; we will tune after 2 weeks of production telemetry.
End-to-end latency for micro-eval run (trigger->composite_score) averaged 2.6 minutes in staging using small worker pool.
Auto-rollback simulation validated traffic switch within 45s and audit entries created correctly in 100% of test runs.
